hotspot_events.heat_reason: §744.24 remote compute access control takes effect today, with a 12 million TPP threshold plus a 90‑day transition period, new licensing requirements for five Southeast Asian countries, putting pressure on Southeast Asian data‑center delivery schedules
hotspot_events.summary: The U.S. BIS interim final rule adds §744.24: when exporting advanced compute items to any data center worldwide, if the data center provides more than 12 million TPP compute access to entities in China, Macau, or the D:5 national‑group headquarters, a license must be obtained, with a 90‑day transition period. Exporting advanced AI items to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil now requires additional licensing. The rule also formally repeals the Biden‑era “AI Export Control Rule.” Singapore says it is “carefully studying the details,” Malaysia says operators must comply and is drafting disclosure legislation, and China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs calls it “typical economic coercion and extraterritorial jurisdiction.”
hotspot_events.title: U.S. BIS New Chip Export Controls Effective Today 11‑19

hotspot_events.summary: The minutes of the Oct 27‑28 meeting (released 03:00 Beijing time on 11‑19) show the October meeting voted 10‑2 to keep the rate at 3.75%–4.00% (after a 25 bp hike in September). “Almost all” participants think a further December hike “may be appropriate,” “several” say that if inflation data worsen, a hike of more than 25 bp could be considered in December, and “many” view AI infrastructure as a substantive inflation risk source. Director Waller on 11‑18 said a 50 bp December hike should be considered; CME shows a ~95% probability of a 25 bp December hike. On 11‑18 the S&P fell 0.23% (five‑day decline), the Nasdaq rose 0.42%, Nvidia closed down 2.89% to $150.96, and spot gold was about $3,757/oz, a new low since September.
